newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on weak peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 45 basis points at 18.75 percent on Tuesday in response to a weaker peso, traders said.
"We opened up from the bell, partly due to the peso and although we receded during the day, we still closed up," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.5 of a centavo softer at 7.7980/7.8010 per dollar.
Traders added that the peso weakened on forecast cuts in primary interest rates at the central bank's weekly auction to be held later in the day.
A Reuters survey nN18546675 of nine money market traders in Mexico City showed they forecast an average fall of 52 basis points for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to 19.17 percent.
This would be the lowest level for 28-day Cetes since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Banco de Mexico is due to release auction results at 1830 local time.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended up 25 basis points at 20.60 pesos.

Banco de Mexico drained 4.798 billion pesos from the market to offset surplus liquidity. Traders said the surplus had originally been calculated at 204 million pesos due to a prior central bank intervention falling due, but government spending flooded the system.
Liquidity of 258 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Wednesday.
